chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ya'qub ibn Shu'ayb, from Husayn ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'In how much time should I recite the Quran?' He said, 'Recite it in fifths, or recite it in sevenths. Indeed, with me there is a Mushaf divided into fourteen parts.'

key_terms.مُصْحَفاً: A codex or copy of the Quran

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended timeframes for reciting the entire Quran according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) outlines permissible timeframes for completing the Quran, suggesting divisions into fifths or sevenths, while also mentioning his personal practice of dividing the Quran into fourteen parts. This hadith highlights the flexibility in recitation schedules, allowing for both shorter and longer periods to complete the Quran. The guidance reflects the practical considerations of balancing devotion with daily life, emphasizing the importance of consistent engagement with the Quran.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhamad Bin Al Husayn, from Ali Bin Al Nu’man, from Yaqoub Bin Shuayb, from Husayn Bin Khalid, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘In how much (time) should I recite the (whole) Quran?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Recite it in fifths or sevenths. But, with me<sup>asws</sup> there is a Parchment sectioned upon fourteen parts’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Nu’Man from Ya’qub ibn Shu’ayb from Husayn ibn Khalid who has said the following:

“Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) ‘In how many days should one complete reading the Holy Quran?’ The Imam said, ‘You may read it in five or seven days. I, however, have a copy of the Holy Quran that is divided into fourteen parts.’”
